subject: chemistry
title: Giant covalent structures: diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide
key_idea: In a giant covalent structure every atom is joined to its neighbours by strong covalent bonds, so the melting points are very high. Diamond and graphite are two forms of carbon. Diamond is hard and does not conduct, while graphite is soft and conducts.

blocks.text: Some covalent substances are not small molecules. This section covers what a giant covalent structure is and why it has a very high melting point.

items.meaning: A very large network of atoms, all joined by covalent bonds.
Different forms of the same element, such as diamond and graphite.
An electron that is not held by one atom and can move through the structure.

items: Diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide (silica) are giant covalent structures.
They are solids with very high melting points.
All the atoms are linked to other atoms by strong covalent bonds.
Many strong bonds must be broken to melt or boil them, so a lot of energy is needed.
Giant covalent structures have very high melting points.
Many strong covalent bonds must be broken, not weak intermolecular forces.
Carbon can form four covalent bonds.

blocks.text: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, but their atoms are arranged differently. This section covers each structure and the properties it gives.

items: Each carbon atom forms **four** covalent bonds with four other carbon atoms.
This makes a giant lattice, a repeating three-dimensional pattern.
It is very hard, because of the many strong bonds throughout the structure. It is used in cutting tools.
It has a very high melting point.
It does not conduct electricity, because all four outer electrons of each atom are used in bonding. No electrons can move.
Each carbon atom forms **three** covalent bonds with three other carbon atoms.
The bonds make layers of hexagonal rings. There are no covalent bonds between the layers.
One electron from each carbon atom is delocalised, so graphite conducts electricity, as a metal does.
The layers can slide over each other because the forces between them are weak. So graphite is soft and slippery.
It has a high melting point, because of the many strong covalent bonds in the layers.

rows: Conducts electricity, and is inert and does not react

items: Diamond: four bonds per carbon, no free electrons, very hard.
Graphite: three bonds per carbon, layers, delocalised electrons.
Graphite conducts and is soft. Diamond does neither.

blocks.text: Silicon dioxide is a third giant covalent structure. This section covers it, and sets all three side by side.

items: Silicon dioxide, SiO₂, is made of silicon and oxygen atoms.
Each silicon atom forms four bonds, and each oxygen atom forms two.
It has a giant structure with strong covalent bonds, so a very high melting point.

All three are giant covalent: strong bonds throughout and very high melting points.
Only graphite conducts, because only graphite has delocalised electrons.

checks.q: Explain why diamond has a very high melting point.
checks.a: The covalent bonds are strong, and many of them must be broken, so a lot of energy is needed.
Each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds, so one electron per atom is delocalised. These electrons can move through the structure and carry charge.

checks.q: Explain why graphite is soft and slippery.
checks.a: It has layers with weak forces between them and no covalent bonds between the layers, so the layers slide over each other.

worked_example.question: Diamond is a form of carbon with a giant covalent structure. Explain why diamond has a very high melting point.
answer_points: Many covalent bonds must be broken.
So a lot of energy is required.
worked_example.tip: One mark each: strong, many, a lot of energy. Do not write about intermolecular forces.

worked_example.question: Diamond and graphite are two forms of carbon. Diamond is one of the hardest known substances on Earth and is used in cutting tools. Graphite is soft and flaky. Diamond is a poor electrical conductor, but graphite is a good electrical conductor. Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, these properties of diamond and graphite.
answer_points: Diamond does not conduct: all four outer electrons of each carbon form covalent bonds, each carbon is joined to four others, so there are no free electrons.
Graphite conducts: three outer electrons form bonds, each carbon is joined to three others, and one electron per atom is delocalised and moves to carry current.
Diamond is hard: strong covalent bonds between all the carbon atoms in a giant 3D lattice need a very high amount of energy to overcome.
Graphite is soft: strong covalent bonds within each layer, but weak forces between the layers, so the layers can slide.
worked_example.tip: A six-mark question is marked by level. Explain all three properties fully using structure and bonding for both substances.

worked_example.question: Graphite can be used as a lubricant because it is slippery. Explain why graphite is slippery. Use ideas about structure and bonding in graphite in your answer.
answer_points: Graphite forms layers of covalently bonded carbon atoms.
There are weak forces between the layers.
The layers can slide or slip over each other.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. A reference to ionic bonds scores zero for the whole question.
